segments.text: This is another in a series of lectures by Swami Ishvara Sarupaji at his ashram on July 5th, 1975.
This will be a continuation of the lectures concerning the Shiva Sutra-Vimarshani, beginning with Sutra number 17.
Yidrak Gyanarupasya, I see Yogina, for such Yogi whose knowledge is highly elevated to him, Vittarka, Atm Gyanam.
Any inference of such a Yogi is knowledge of his own real self, whatever he thinks, whatever he confirms that is one with the knowledge of one's own self.
For such a Yogi, not for everybody, but generally he thinks Vishwathma, Shiva, Ava, Asmi.
This is his perception for all the time that I am Lord Shiva, one with universe, Vishwathma, Shiva, Ava, Asmi.
This kind of Vittarka, Vittarka means perception, that is Vichar, this is his knowledge, this is his personal knowledge.
Asmi Gyanam means personal knowledge, this is also quoted in Vigyanabhairava.
Permission is all knowing and doer of the whole universe and pervades the whole universe, Vyapaka.
And that Permission is one with myself, because the aspects of Shiva are the aspects of mind for such a Yogi.
By this attentive perception or attentive to meditation, one becomes one with Shiva.
In Spanda also, it is said, I am Ava, Aatmanu, Graha.
This is said to be the real one point in theness of thought.
In this Shloka of Spanda, the knowledge of oneself is that, yet Vishwathma, Shiva, Ava, Ava.
Just becoming one with universal eye, his individual eye becomes one with universal eye.
This in this way, the second meaning also of this Shloka is accepted by our masters.
Vittarka means ordinary perception. Vittarka means Visheshina.
